# 2. Data Audit

```{r}
colSums(is.na(hotels_raw))
# the only na values in the whole dataset are 4 observations in'children'
 
# however, when also checking for NULL or Undefined, we discover a lot more missing values
sapply(hotels_raw, function(x) sum(is.na(x) | x %in% c("NULL", "Undefined", "na")))

# Checking for odd values:

# reservations with 0 guests
sum(hotels_raw$adults + hotels_raw$children + hotels_raw$babies == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
# negative nightly rate 
sum(hotels_raw$adr < 0)        

# extreme nightly rate
sum(hotels_raw$adr > 1000)   
```

## Visualizations

```{r}
# Used AI to help streamline this process
cat_vars <- c("hotel", "meal", "market_segment", "distribution_channel",
              "deposit_type", "customer_type", "reserved_room_type",
              "is_repeated_guest", "arrival_date_month", "country", "agent")

for (v in cat_vars) {
    p <- ggplot(hotels_raw, aes(x = .data[[v]], fill = factor(is_canceled))) +
        geom_bar() +
        labs(title = v, x = NULL, fill = "Canceled") +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
    print(p)
}
```

```{r}
num_vars <- c("lead_time", "adr", "total_nights", "total_guests",
              "previous_cancellations", "previous_bookings_not_canceled",
              "days_in_waiting_list", "required_car_parking_spaces",
              "total_of_special_requests")

for (v in num_vars) {
    p <- ggplot(hotels_raw, aes(x = .data[[v]], fill = factor(is_canceled))) +
        geom_histogram(bins = 40) +
        labs(title = v, fill = "Canceled")
    print(p)
}
```
